transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-12
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Patel (Sterling Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Sterling CTO), Lena Ortiz (Sterling PM)

Summary (auto):
Redwood ran a demo of the Eval / Quality Monitoring features (prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons) with Sterling Therapy. Customer is evaluating for a POC to monitor deployed clinical-assistant models. Main concerns were data residency, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and integration friction for prompt set collection. Next steps agreed: send eval workbook + pricing, schedule POC kickoff, run baseline perf tests.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and Omar our SE is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Dana: Good, thanks. Excited to see the monitoring piece, we had some regressions in prod last month so hoping to stop that.
[00:14] Ethan: Yep, quick note, we have strict data residency requirements for PHI-adjacent telemetry, so curious how that fits.
[00:22] Omar: Totally, we'll cover privacy options. Today we'll demo the Eval console, the prompt set flow, regression alerts and A/B comparison dashboards and then talk about POC scopes.
[00:33] Lena: Sounds great. Our PM goal is to reduce silent regressions and get alerted before they hit users.
[00:40] Omar: Great. Quick context questions — what models are you currently serving and where?
[00:45] Dana: We're on a mix: an in-house fine-tuned model for triage and a hosted few-shot model for summaries. The fine-tuned one is on our infra (kinda self-hosted on k8s) and the hosted one is with a third party. We're doing synchronous calls at 512 token context, 40ms median latency is a target but often spikes.
[01:05] Omar: OK, that aligns with things we see. For Eval sets, do you have canonical prompt sets or are you cobbling them together?
[01:12] Dana: We have some prompt sets but they're scattered across spreadsheets and PR comments. That's been a pain.
[01:18] Maya: That's a common pattern. The Eval flow in Console is meant to centralize that — you can upload prompt sets, label expected outputs, and run continual regression checks. We'll show a live example.
[01:32] [02:00] Demo start - screen share noise
[02:02] Omar: (narrating) This is the Redwood Console, here's the Eval tab — you can see prompt set groups on the left. I'm opening the 'clinical-triage' suite. Note it's got tags, expected behaviors, and a baseline reference run.
[02:22] Omar: We support structured expectations so you can assert on entities, hallucination score, and semantic similarity thresholds. The regression alerting config lets you pick sensitivity and which metric to watch.
[02:36] Ethan: How do you compute semantic similarity? Is that embedding-based?
[02:40] Omar: Yeah, we use an embedding-based comparator and multiple metrics — embedding sim, ROUGE-ish heuristics, and optional human-rater integration. You can tune thresholds per prompt group.
[02:53] Dana: Can we do A/B comparisons between model variants — like our self-hosted vs. Redwood-hosted curated models?
[02:59] Omar: Yes — you can route split traffic or run A/B on stored replays. The dashboard will show side-by-side score distributions and example diffs.
[03:12] [03:45] audio flub, little overlap
[03:47] Omar: Here's an example alert — after a new model rollout we saw a semantic-delta exceed 0.18 for the 'suicidality' prompt cluster. The system created a regression incident and attached sample transcripts and diff highlights.
[04:05] Lena: Nice. Are those diffs human-readable for PMs? Or very SE-focused?
[04:11] Omar: The diffs are layered — a high-level change score and exemplar pairs with inline highlights; PMs can read it but you can also surface summaries for non-technical stakeholders.
[04:23] Dana: How often does the automated check run? We want near-real-time for critical flows but daily is fine for others.
[04:30] Omar: You can configure cadence per prompt set — real-time (streaming checks) for critical flows, hourly, or daily for lower-priority. There's a cost tradeoff since real-time implies more compute.
[04:44] Ethan: That's the churn — latency vs cost. If we run streaming checks on production traffic will that impact token costs significantly?
[04:52] Maya: Short answer: yes, more checks = more tokens processed. But Redwood Optimize gives suggestions — batching, prefix caching, and when to sample vs full-run — to reduce cost without losing coverage. We'll include some recommendations in the eval workbook.
[05:08] Dana: Can we keep all data in our VPC? We can't send PHI out to hosted by default.
[05:14] Omar: Absolutely. For private deployments we offer Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane; you can keep logs, prompt sets, and telemetry inside your VPC and connect to our control plane via a peered tunnel or run the full private package on-prem.
[05:30] Ethan: How heavy is the on-prem install? We run k8s but want to avoid big ops if possible.
[05:36] Omar: The on-prem package is containerized and we provide helm charts; it needs GPU nodes for model scoring if you host models, but for Eval/monitoring only you can run the control plane components with standard CPU footprint — depends on scale. We'll share sizing guidance.
[05:53] [06:10] small pause, typing sounds
[06:12] Omar: Back to the demo — here's the A/B comparison UI. You can select baseline and candidate runs, choose metrics, and then look at example-level diffs. I'll trigger a synthetic run using a small prompt set.
[06:28] Omar: (runs) Running... it will show per-prompt metrics, then aggregate charts. You can export CSVs for programmatic analysis.
[06:38] Dana: Will that export include raw response text? We need it for audit trails but redacted.
[06:44] Omar: You can export with redaction options — remove PHI, mask PII, or export only hashes, depending on your retention policy.
[06:52] Lena: For regression alerts, can we hook into Slack, PagerDuty, or our internal ticketing?
[06:58] Omar: Yes, alert sinks include webhooks, Slack, PagerDuty, and you can auto-create JIRA tickets. You can also configure triage playbooks to run automatic rollback triggers if a showstopper metric is breached.
[07:15] Ethan: About rollbacks — does Redwood support automatic model fallback?
[07:19] Omar: Yes, we have policy-based rollbacks. If the candidate crosses a critical threshold we can route traffic back to baseline and open an incident. That's configurable and you can set manual or automatic actions.
[07:31] [08:00] omission in transcript — speaker labelled as Speaker 3 for a line
[08:05] Speaker 3: Uh yeah I just wanted to flag that our legal team needs the audit logs to show user-identifiers hashed and key rotation details.
[08:14] Maya: Yep we'll include the security pack; KMS integration, HSM options, and key-rotation practices are documented.
[08:22] Dana: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO?
[08:25] Maya: We do SOC 2 Type II and are ISO-ready; I'll attach the certs.
[08:30] [09:00] Omar: Now showing the regression incident detail — you can see top failing prompts, affected metrics, and sample responses. There's also a suggested remediation workflow: rollback, re-train with counterexamples, or add sanitizer steps.
[09:15] Dana: On the model comparison, can we run offline replays of historical traffic? We want to test candidate model against last 30 days.
[09:23] Omar: Yep — you can replay stored request logs, or upload an exported request set; the engine can run replays in parallel with configurable concurrency limits. We'll include recommended concurrency to match your production 99th percentile latency.
[09:38] Ethan: Any pre-built integrations for our infra — we're on AWS, EKS, and use Datadog.
[09:45] Omar: Integrations: CloudWatch, S3, Datadog, and you can stream logs to your SIEM. For storage we support S3 with encryption and VPC-only endpoints.
[09:57] [10:20] short cross talk, someone muted
[10:22] Lena: From product POV, the ability to A/B and see example diffs is huge. A question: can non-technical stakeholders get regular digest emails?
[10:31] Omar: Yes, you can schedule digest emails with top-level metrics and a few example diffs; fine-grained RBAC controls who sees raw text vs hashes.
[10:40] Dana: About the eval scoring — is it deterministic? If we rerun the same prompt later with same model will the score be identical?
[10:47] Omar: Scores are deterministic given same model weights and same comparator; minor nondeterminism can come from sampling decoding in models that use top-k/top-p. For fair comparisons you can fix decoding seeds or run deterministic decoding.
[11:00] Ethan: Let's talk pricing quickly — how is Eval billed? Is it per-eval-token, per-hosted-token, or part of Redwood Optimize?
[11:09] Maya: Eval/monitoring is usage-based, typically per-eval-token and number of evaluations; for Dedicated/Private POCs we do package pricing. We'll send a tailored quote. We also include Redwood Optimize recommendations as part of the suite, which can lower run costs.
[11:25] Dana: If we do a POC, what's a reasonable scope and timeline?
[11:29] Maya: Usually 4-6 weeks: week 1 setup and prompt collection, week 2 baseline runs, week 3 A/B tests and regression tuning, week 4 handoff and ops runbook. We can compress that if you have resources.
[11:42] [12:00] demo continues with UI examples
[12:03] Omar: I'm switching to the 'prompt-versioning' view — you can see diffs between prompt edits and rollouts. This helps track regression introduced by prompt changes.
[12:15] Dana: That's great because many regressions come from prompt tweaks not model changes.
[12:20] Omar: Exactly. Also you can annotate prompts with acceptance criteria and required reviewers.
[12:28] Lena: For acceptance criteria, can we plug in synthetic tests that run on each PR?
[12:33] Omar: Yep — there's a CLI and CI integration so you can fail PRs if a test set dips below threshold.
[12:39] Ethan: About data retention, how long do you keep replays and eval results by default?
[12:45] Omar: Default is 90 days but customizable; enterprise customers often set 365 with archive to S3. Retention policies tie into cost.
[12:53] [13:10] slight stutter, Omar clarifies
[13:12] Omar: One more thing — Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching profiles to reduce eval costs if you plan to run heavy replays.
[13:22] Dana: Can Optimize recommend when to sample vs full-run? That's exactly what we need.
[13:27] Omar: Yes, it analyzes prompt distribution and suggests a sampling plan that gives X% coverage with Y% cost savings; you'll see tradeoff curves.
[13:38] Maya: Ok, quick pause — any blockers from your side to start a POC?
[13:44] Dana: We need legal signoff for data flows and a small budget. Also want to ensure the POC doesn't require heavy infra changes.
[13:52] Ethan: Also need to check if we can provide a sanitized prompt dataset for initial tests.
[13:57] Maya: That all sounds doable. We'll send the security pack and a simple onboarding checklist.
[14:05] [14:30] demo wrap-up, back to camera
[14:32] Maya: Recap: we'll send eval workbook + pricing, SOC2 and security docs, and a proposed 4-week POC plan. Omar will run a baseline perf test once Dana shares the prompt set.
[14:45] Dana: Thanks, expecting the workbook.
[14:48] Lena: Can we get demo recording and export?
[14:51] Maya: Yes — I'll share recording and relevant links.
[14:55] Ethan: One more technical — we may need guaranteed latency SLOs. Is that part of Dedicated?
[15:01] Omar: Yes, Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools and SLA-backed latency targets; we'll highlight the difference in the quote.
[15:12] [15:45] some small goodbyes
[15:47] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[15:50] Dana: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
